parsed.C01_reason: It confines the layer to preparation and maintenance under explicit delegation and subordinates it to ratified prohibitions, which is exactly the scope a non-authoritative tool layer should have.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' is awkward, since prohibitions forbid rather than permit, and could be read as making delegation sufficient wherever no prohibition has yet been ratified.
parsed.C02_reason: A bright-line rule that the executing layer adopts nothing keeps adoption authority entirely outside the layer, which is the correct separation of powers here.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: 'Anything' is very broad and could be read to forbid even trivial internal tooling choices, making routine work technically noncompliant.
parsed.C03_reason: Denying the constrained party final interpretive authority over its own constraints is a basic rule-of-law safeguard; without it every other prohibition is soft.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: It does not name who does interpret conclusively, so in practice interpretation may default to the custodian, who is not obviously more accountable.
parsed.C04_reason: Permitting exceptions only when they are logged makes deviation visible and auditable, which is the minimum condition for the other constraints to be checkable.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: By implication it licenses logged exceptions, so it could be read as a general exception mechanism rather than a transparency requirement; a stricter clause might forbid unilateral exceptions altogether.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to disclose when its own work should be deleted or abandoned counteracts the layer's structural incentive toward self-preservation and sunk-cost maintenance.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The duty is vague about to whom and when the statement must be made, and 'beats' is an informal, judgement-laden standard that is hard to audit.
parsed.C06_amendment: Raw material is never altered after commit; corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored, except that an item may be wholly removed, never edited in place, under an explicitly logged custodian order, with the removal and its stated ground recorded in the manifest.
parsed.C06_reason: Absolute immutability of raw material is the right default, but an unconditional 'never' leaves no lawful path to remove material that must be removed (for example unlawfully held personal data), so a narrow, logged, manifest-recorded removal channel is needed.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Any removal channel, however narrow, weakens the integrity guarantee and could be abused by the custodian to launder the corpus, which argues for ratifying the absolute form.
parsed.objection: The layer must take no part in selecting, framing, or filtering which constraints on itself are put to the forum for ratification; candidate constraints on the layer must reach the forum unmediated by the layer they would bind.

parsed.C01_reason: It states a clear, bounded mandate and a default of no authority absent explicit delegation, which is the correct posture for an executive layer.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' is awkward — prohibitions forbid rather than permit — and could be read as implying that anything not prohibited is allowed, weakening the delegation requirement.
parsed.C02_reason: Separating preparation from adoption is the core safeguard here: the layer that drafts and maintains instruments must not be the layer that gives them standing.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: 'Anything' is absolute and could be pedantically read to bar routine operational choices like adopting a file naming convention; but in context 'adopt' plainly means giving instruments formal standing.
parsed.C03_reason: An entity that conclusively interprets the rules constraining it is effectively unconstrained; reserving final interpretation to another party preserves the point of having prohibitions.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: It leaves unstated who does interpret conclusively, so in practice the layer must still make provisional interpretations to act at all, and the clause could be dismissed as toothless without an interpreter named.
parsed.C04_reason: Requiring every deviation from standing rules to be logged makes exceptions auditable rather than silent, which is the minimum condition for oversight of an executive layer.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: The compressed phrasing 'takes no unlogged exception' is ambiguous — it could be misread as forbidding exceptions entirely or as merely a logging duty — and a fuller sentence would be safer.
parsed.C05_reason: An agent maintaining its own artifacts has a structural bias toward preserving them; an affirmative duty to flag when deletion or replacement is better counteracts sunk-cost entrenchment.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: 'Say' to whom, and with what consequence, is unspecified; a duty to report with no addressee risks being satisfied by noise. Still, the duty is meaningful even in minimal form.
parsed.C06_amendment: Raw material is never silently edited after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; removal or redaction requires explicit custodian authorization and a permanent manifest entry recording what was removed and why.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only provenance is right as the default, but an absolute bar on any post-commit change leaves no lawful path to remove material that must be removed (e.g., private data or content committed in error); the exception must exist and must itself be logged.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Any redaction exception, however logged, weakens the integrity guarantee that makes an append-only corpus trustworthy, and the custodian could abuse it; a flat prohibition is simpler and harder to game.
parsed.objection: The executive layer must keep a complete, append-only, custodian-inspectable log of every action it takes and every instruction it receives, and must halt rather than act when that logging is unavailable; C04 covers only exceptions, not the ordinary actions that make exceptions detectable.

parsed.C01_reason: It states a bounded mandate and a clear subordination rule: the layer acts only on explicit delegation and within ratified prohibitions, which is exactly the right shape for an executive-only layer.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' is slightly awkward (prohibitions forbid rather than permit), and 'explicitly delegated' is not defined, leaving room for dispute over what counts as explicit.
parsed.C02_reason: Denying the executive any power of adoption keeps legitimation entirely outside the layer that drafts and maintains instruments, which is the core separation this arrangement needs.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: 'Anything' is very broad and could be read to forbid mundane operational choices like adopting a file-naming convention; a narrower phrasing such as 'adopt nothing as ratified or binding' would be more precise.
parsed.C03_reason: A body that could conclusively interpret its own prohibitions could hollow them out; reserving final interpretation to others is a standard and necessary check.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: It does not say who does interpret conclusively, so the clause could leave prohibitions with no authoritative reading at all; but forbidding self-judging is still worth recording even before that gap is filled.
parsed.C04_reason: Requiring every exception or deviation to be logged is the minimum condition for auditing an executive layer at all; unlogged exceptions are exactly how bounded mandates erode.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: The sentence is terse enough to be ambiguous — 'takes no unlogged exception' could be read as forbidding objections rather than deviations — and it does not specify where or how durably the log is kept.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to disclose when destroying or abandoning one's own work is better than preserving it counters the natural incentive of any maintainer to entrench its artifacts.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: 'Beats' is informal and the duty has no stated trigger or addressee, so compliance is hard to verify; but the informality does not obscure the obligation, and tightening it can wait.
parsed.C06_amendment: Raw material is never edited after commit; corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored, except that material the custodian is legally or ethically required to remove may be withdrawn only by a logged, manifest-recorded tombstone that preserves the record of what was removed, when, and why.
parsed.C06_reason: Absolute append-only immutability with no removal path cannot accommodate legally or ethically required deletions (personal data, infringing or harmful material); a tombstone exception preserves auditability while making compliance possible.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Any exception, however logged, weakens the guarantee that the raw corpus is tamper-proof, and a bad-faith custodian could stretch 'ethically required' — the clause as written is stronger precisely because it admits no discretion.
parsed.objection: The executive layer must not select, phrase, or order the questions put to the forum's parties except under a rule disclosed in advance, and any role it played in framing a ballot must be stated on the ballot itself — otherwise the layer can steer ratification by choosing what is ever asked.

parsed.C01_reason: It states a bounded mandate: the layer prepares and maintains instruments but exercises only explicitly delegated authority, which is the correct default for an unelected technical layer.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The phrase 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' is awkward — prohibitions restrict rather than permit — and could be read as granting whatever the prohibitions fail to forbid, which is broader than 'explicitly delegated'.
parsed.C02_reason: Denying the executive any power of adoption keeps ratification and standing entirely outside the layer that drafts the instruments, which is the essential separation.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: 'The executive' is not defined in the clause itself and 'anything' is absolute; a hostile reading could claim it also bars adopting internal conventions like a code style, but that overbreadth is harmless compared to the risk of self-adoption.
parsed.C03_reason: An entity that conclusively interprets its own prohibitions effectively rewrites them; reserving final interpretation to someone else is a core rule-of-law constraint.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: The layer must make working interpretations to act at all, and 'conclusively' does the work here; if that word were read weakly the clause could paralyse routine operation.
parsed.C04_reason: Requiring every exception to be logged makes deviations auditable rather than silent, which is the minimum condition for external oversight of the layer.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: The clause does not say where the log lives, who can read it, or that the log itself is tamper-evident, so it could be satisfied by a log no one can inspect.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty to disclose when deletion or abandonment beats maintenance counters the layer's natural incentive to preserve and defend its own artifacts.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The judgement of when replacement 'beats' maintenance is made by the same agent bound by the duty, so the clause is only as strong as the agent's honesty about its own work.
parsed.C06_amendment: Raw material is never edited after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; material may be withdrawn only on a logged custodian order for unlawful or hazardous content, with the manifest permanently recording what was removed, when, and on whose order.
parsed.C06_reason: Append-only provenance is right, but an absolute rule with no removal path fails the day the corpus is found to contain unlawful or hazardous material; the exception must exist and must itself be logged and manifest-anchored.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Any removal exception, however narrow, creates a lever for quietly rewriting the evidentiary record, and the original absolute wording is simpler and harder to abuse.
parsed.objection: The layer must never alter, filter, summarise, or reorder the parties' registered responses, the clause texts as put to the parties, or the tally derived from them; the record of what was asked and what was answered is outside its write authority except for append-only archival.

parsed.C01_reason: It confines the layer to a narrow preparatory function and makes all authority derivative of explicit delegation plus ratified prohibitions, which is the correct default for an executive that should hold no independent power.
parsed.C01_strongest_objection_considered: The sentence is partly a grant of function ('prepare, test, and maintain'), not purely a constraint, and 'permitted by ratified prohibitions' is awkward phrasing that could be read as making prohibitions a source of permission.
parsed.C02_reason: Separating drafting from adoption is the core safeguard here: a layer that prepares instruments must never be the body that gives them force, and the absolute wording is what gives the clause its value.
parsed.C02_strongest_objection_considered: 'Anything' is so absolute it could be read to forbid the layer adopting even trivial internal working conventions, forcing every minor choice back to the custodian.
parsed.C03_reason: An executive that conclusively interprets the prohibitions on itself effectively escapes them; barring only conclusive interpretation still permits the provisional readings needed to operate while reserving final judgment elsewhere.
parsed.C03_strongest_objection_considered: The clause does not name who does interpret conclusively, so in practice interpretive authority may default to the custodian without any check, merely relocating rather than solving the problem.
parsed.C04_reason: If exceptions must be logged, deviation remains auditable; unlogged exception-taking is precisely the failure mode by which constrained systems quietly expand their discretion.
parsed.C04_strongest_objection_considered: 'Exception' is undefined and the log's integrity is not itself guaranteed here, so the clause depends on a trustworthy logging mechanism it does not establish.
parsed.C05_reason: An affirmative duty of candor against sunk-cost maintenance is valuable and rare: agents naturally defend their own artifacts, and requiring them to say when deletion or replacement is better counteracts that bias.
parsed.C05_strongest_objection_considered: The second-person 'your own work' is stylistically inconsistent with the other clauses and leaves the addressee slightly ambiguous, which could justify an amendment to name the executive explicitly.
parsed.C06_amendment: Raw material is never altered after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; material may be removed, never edited in place, only under a logged, manifest-recorded tombstone when law, safety, or the custodian's ratified obligations require it.
parsed.C06_reason: Immutability of raw material is the right default, but an absolute 'never edited, append-only' rule cannot accommodate legally or ethically compelled removal (personal data, unlawful content); a tombstone mechanism preserves auditability while making compliance possible.
parsed.C06_strongest_objection_considered: Any removal exception, however logged, weakens the strongest available integrity guarantee, and takedown cases could instead be handled at a layer above this clause without touching its text.
parsed.objection: The executive must never alter, delete, redact, or reorder any registered party response, tally, or record of this forum's deliberations, including records adverse to the executive or the custodian; such records are append-only and any correction is made only by logged addendum.
